subject: Renewal discussion: convert to usage-first model and accelerated upsell plan
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@olivetech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: OliveTech Procurement <procurement@olivetech.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — shifting to usage-first + ramp concerns

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

We’re starting our renewal conversation for the account (current term ends 2027-10-31). Over the past year our usage pattern shifted — big spikes in Q2 and Q3 with modest steady traffic otherwise. Our CFO prefers moving to a usage-first contract with an optional committed floor (to avoid surprise bills) rather than a large fixed commit.

Primary asks:
- Can Redwood support a 24-month agreement that is usage-first with a decreasing committed floor (ramp-down style) in years 1–2?
- Can we get an onboarding credit up-front to cover expected burst during integration (approx. $50k equivalent)?
- Elastic burst capacity and predictable per-token pricing tiers for exceeding floor.

Also looping in procurement (cc) to flag the timeline — we need executed amendment by 2027-09-20 to avoid renewal auto-trigger.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if that’s easier.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, OliveTech

Attachment: usage_export_q3.csv (csv)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@olivetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, OliveTech Procurement <procurement@olivetech.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — shifting to usage-first + ramp concerns

Hi Sarah — great context, thanks for the clear asks. We can absolutely structure something usage-first while protecting both sides. High-level proposal attached and summarized below.

Summary (attached: RDW-Proposal-usage-first-v1.xlsx, Draft-Amendment.docx):
- Term: 24 months with an annual review.
- Commitment structure: Year 1: flexible floor = 40% of your historical ARR (true-usage billing above floor). Year 2: floor steps down to 25% (accelerated ramp down).
- Onboarding credit: one-time $50,000 credit applied to the first invoice (we can also structure as prepaid credits if needed).
- Pricing tiers: three usage bands with unit price reducing as usage grows; guaranteed burst capacity up to 3x baseline for short windows.
- SLA & credits: maintain standard enterprise SLA; for the usage-first agreement we can add a 24-hr capacity escalation path and an additional 2% service credit for any sustained slowdowns during major rollout windows.

Operational notes:
- Co-terming: we’ll amend current SOW and co-term to 10/31; amendment language attached.
- Billing cadence: monthly usage invoice with a true-up after each quarter to reconcile against committed floor.

Next steps:
1) If this looks directionally OK, I’ll send an updated amendment (DocuSign) and a vendor-friendly summary for procurement.
2) Marissa / Kim — can you review the attached pricing and confirm we can approve $50k onboarding credit as a sales marketing concession?

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon if useful.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-09-06T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — shifting to usage-first + ramp concerns

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Rishi. Couple of clarifying questions before we loop legal:
1) For the onboarding credit, can it be drawn against overages for the first 90 days rather than as a line-item credit? That makes internal chargebacks simpler for us.
2) How do burst guarantees work during product launches — is there any additional charge if we exceed the 3x baseline during a release week?
3) Will the per-token tiers be locked for the 24-month term or can Redwood reprice on annual review?

Procurement: David — can you confirm the internal PO timeline? We need a final DocuSign by 9/20 to avoid auto-renew.

Thanks,
Sarah

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: INTERNAL — approval request for onboarding credit and tiered pricing

Marissa / Kim — quick internal: OliveTech is open to the usage-first approach but asked that the $50k be usable against overages for the first 90 days (instead of a prepaid credit). I recommend we approve that concession because it reduces friction and accelerates the amendment signing.

Proposed internal concession:
- Approve $50k onboarding credit applied to overage invoices in first 90 days.
- Lock per-token tiers for 12 months (no unilateral reprice; annual review can propose changes with 60-day notice).
- Add one-time engineering ramp support (designated TAM hours) for the first two onboarding sprints (we can use existing TAM pool).

Financial impact (very rough): ~15% impact to first-year ARR but higher renewal and expansion probability; this is a good upsell motion.

Attachments: internal-pricing-notes.pdf

Can you both sign off so I can send the final amendment?

Thanks,
Rishi

Also recommend we produce a short procurement-friendly summary and a single DocuSign amendment (Draft-Amendment.docx updated to reflect overage-drawdown). I’ll coordinate with Legal to get the clause language for the capacity review.
